thread:
infra-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Multiple nodes in inference-pool-usw transitioning to NotReady (3 nodes) — automated page created. Pod evictions detected, several inference pods restarting. Paging on-call.

ryan_oncall: Acked. I'm on it. What's the initial signal? CPU? kubelet?

infra-bot: kubelet heartbeats missed; messages show kubelet restart loops and 'node not ready' events. Sample events: 
```
Warning  NodeNotReady  2m   kubelet  Node not ready: kubelet stopped posting status
Warning  Evicted      2m   kubelet  Pod eviction due to node pressure
```

maya_runtime: I'm seeing CUDA driver complaints in the node logs right before kubelet restarts. Here's a tail from /var/log/kern.log on one affected node (node-id: i-usw-gpu-12):
```
[11:22:01] NVRM: GPU 0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[11:22:03] systemd: kubelet.service: main process exited, code=exited, status=1/FAILURE
[11:22:05] dockerd: containerd: failed to create shim: OCI runtime create failed: runc create failed: container_linux.go:...
```

alex_sre: That 'fallen off the bus' message usually points at driver/firmware flakiness or hardware resets. Could also be OOM-induced GPU reset. Any OOM events?

maya_runtime: Not seeing kernel OOM yet, but dmesg has repeated GPU reset logs. Also seeing a bunch of pods with status CrashLoopBackOff with stderr showing CUDA driver init errors.

jess_csr: We're already getting alerts from a handful of customers — increased 5xx rate on hosted-api routes for large-token generations. I've correlated to these region tags (us-west-2) and inference model variants pinned to GPU nodes. Customer support notified.

ryan_oncall: Ok first triage plan: 1) Isolate affected nodes (cordon) 2) Drain non-critical pods to free up nodes 3) Restart kubelet / check driver status 4) Ramp traffic away from inference-pool-usw to fallback pool. I'll coordinate with platform-ops for routing.

platform-ops: We can shift traffic at the routing layer. Initiating temporary route-policy to prefer inference-pool-usw-b to soak traffic. ETA ~2m.

deploy-bot: Routing change applied: preference weight 0.2 -> 0.8 to fallback pool.

ryan_oncall: Good. Executing cordon and drain for the three nodes. Commands: 
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-usw-12
kubectl drain gpu-node-usw-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force
```
Draining now; some pods will be evicted and rescheduled to other pools.

alex_sre: Before we move all traffic, note that draining will temporarily increase load on fallback nodes. Watch latency. Consider reducing concurrency / model size for a few routes.

maya_runtime: I'm connecting to node i-usw-gpu-12 for driver introspection. Quick checks: 
```
ssh core@i-usw-gpu-12 sudo nvidia-smi -q | grep 'Driver Version'
sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 200
```
Driver shows 535.x, and immediately before the crash I see kernel message about a firmware timeout on the GPU. Suspect hardware/firmware.

ryan_oncall: If it's hardware, we'll want to mark the node for reprovision. For immediate mitigation we should: 1) Reimage or stop scheduling to that AZ; 2) Scale up ephemeral fallback pool (dedicated spare capacity) by +2 GPU nodes. Can infra scale that now?

platform-ops: K8s autoscaler won't add GPUS automatically (we have reserved capacity). We can spin up two spare nodes from our warm pool — doing that now, provisioning estimate 3-4 mins.

jess_csr: Noted. I'll update affected customers: ETA for mitigation is ~10-15m; mention we're rerouting traffic and investigating GPU resets.

maya_runtime: Quick workaround to reduce 5xx rate: enable model-fallback to CPU-quantized variant for non-latency-sensitive routes. Patch below (applied via routing control plane):
```
routes.update('text-generation-large', {fallback_model: 'ggml-quant-cpu-v1', traffic_pct: 30})
```
That should drop GPU pressure while keeping throughput.

ryan_oncall: Good call. Apply only to lower priority customers first.

infra-bot: Node gpu-node-usw-12 drained successfully, kubelet still failing to stay up after restart. Systemd shows repeated restarts.

alex_sre: Let's try a controlled node reboot and reimage if kernel driver persists. Commands run: 
```
sudo systemctl restart kubelet || sudo reboot
# if reboot doesn't help
# trigger reimage: /usr/local/bin/provisioner reprovision --node gpu-node-usw-12 --image gpu-base-2025-03
```
Proceeding with reboot now.

maya_runtime: Reboot happened; on recheck nvidia-smi shows GPU detected but with a warning about ECC errors. Kernel logs show a single firmware timeout then recovered. I'm going to leave node cordoned and mark for deeper postmortem hardware test.

platform-ops: Warm-pool nodes are up and registered; pods rescheduled. Traffic shift completed. Observability: 5xx rate dropped from 4.2% -> 0.8% for affected routes. Latency bumped by ~20ms on fallback pool.

jess_csr: Customers on initial page updated: most seeing improved behavior. A couple still report errors on batch-heavy jobs. Marking as 'partial mitigation'.

ryan_oncall: Next steps: - Keep the three original nodes cordoned and schedule reprovisioning for two of them. - Run full burn-in on warm-pool nodes for 30m. - Keep routing preference in place until we hit steady state. - Open incident and assign to eng-runtime for driver/firmware investigation.

maya_runtime: Creating an incident ticket and attaching kernel/NVRM logs, CUDA error traces, and nvidia-smi dumps. Recommended action: firmware update for the GPU nodes and expand driver watchdog timeout. Will coordinate with hardware vendor.

alex_sre: For immediate prevention, I'm adding a temporary kubelet restart-backoff policy tweak to reduce oscillation on driver resets (increase RestartSec to 30s) and enabling a prestart healthcheck script to validate nvidia-smi before accepting pods. Patch applied to node groups as a daemonset: 
```
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata:
  name: gpu-health-check
spec: ...
```

platform-ops: Rolling canary of the healthcheck daemonset to 10% of GPU nodes started.

ryan_oncall: We're in monitoring window. Keeping the thread open. If anything regresses, tag @ryan_oncall and escalate to paging escalation policy to oncall-sre-lead.

jess_csr: Noted. I'll continue to update customers and close their pages as they confirm recovery.

infra-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Partial mitigation achieved. Routing fallback in place, 2 warm-pool nodes active. Affected nodes cordoned and reprovision scheduled.

platform-ops: Plan for post-incident: run hardware diagnostics on the three nodes, coordinate vendor firmware rollout, and add capacity to warm-pool by +1 permanently.

maya_runtime: I'll follow up with a detailed postmortem doc and include reproducible trigger logs, suggested driver config changes, and tests for firmware regressions.

ryan_oncall: Thanks team. Good coordination. Marking for incident handoff to eng-runtime for root cause and long-term remediation. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Thread closed by ryan_oncall at 2470001420.
